messages:
ben: Draft RFC: request-fencing + retry-insurance for edge proxy. TL;DR: add a compact per-request fence header + a server-managed retry-insurance token so midstream hedges/replays can be proven-safe. doc: https://go/rfc/fence-retry-insurance CC @marta @aj

marta: skimmed. curious how this differs from idempotency-key flow we already use for non-streaming requests. is it just an extra lease?

ben: right question. differences: 1) fences are short-lived binding to an active stream (not long-lived idempotency keys). 2) retry-insurance token is opaque server-side proof that a replay won't double-apply side effects — it's tied to the fence+backend-commit-checkpoint.

aj: sketch: client sets X-Redwood-Fence: <uuid>. ingress binds fence -> session lease. if we detect a midstream reconnect we check lease ownership, then consult retry-insurance to permit replay. if backend already accepted a terminal commit, insurance rejects.

nina: how do we prevent memory blow-up from holding many fences + KV caches? we can’t keep large amounts per-tenant indefinitely.

ben: proposals in doc: fence TTL defaults to 5s after last active frame; renewal allowed up to 60s for long-running responses; eviction heuristics: LRU per-tenant + global soft cap. also snapshot minimal metadata only (fence id, last-token-index, backend-commit-id).

talia: what about streaming abort visibility? if client cancels, do we immediately release the fence? what if client reconnects quickly and wants resume?

ben: good point. we want rapid release for resource fairness but also a short grace window to allow benign reconnects. suggested flow: on cancel from client we mark fence as "soft-cancel" and start a 2s grace timer. during grace: reconnect with same fence can resume. after grace timer we mark fence as "closed" and start TTL purge.

aj: edge case: partial response delivered to client, then client retries with same fence and our upstream already committed side-effect. insurance must allow idempotent re-run or short-circuit. how do we signal replay outcome to the client?

ben: insurance token encodes (server-verified) outcome categories: ALLOW_REPLAY (backend not committed), SHORT_CIRCUIT (commit observed, return cached final), FORBID (unsafe). client sees status via trailer header: `X-Redwood-Retry-Result: SHORT_CIRCUIT|ALLOW_REPLAY|FORBID`.

marta: do we need telemetry hooks? I want counters: fence_created, fence_reused, fence_evicted, replay_allowed, replay_forbidden, short_circuit_hits. also latency bucket for resume vs new.

nina: test plan: fuzz reconnections, simulate backend commit races, check no double-side-effects. add unit tests for TTL/renewal paths and load tests that exercise LRU eviction under heavy tenant load.

aj: implementation sketch (edge proxy): 1) accept X-Redwood-Fence and optional X-Redwood-Client-Resume boolean 2) on incoming stream open, try bindFence(fenceId, sessionId) 3) if bind fails and insurance token present, call insurance.allowReplay(token, fenceId) 4) forward to backend with `X-Redwood-Fence` & `X-Redwood-Fence-Seq` frames 5) on backend commit event, store commit-id in fence record and emit insurance token to client

ben: quick config snippet for operators:

```
edge.fence:
  default_ttl_ms: 5000
  grace_ms: 2000
  max_tenant_fences: 200
  global_soft_cap: 20000
```

aj: question about cross-region: fences must be global if clients may hit different frontdoors. do we replicate fence state or prefer sticky routing?

ben: proposal: prefer sticky routing (session affinity) for active fenced streams. replicate minimal commit annotations to a small cross-region KV with async propagation for short-lived fences. only promote to global replicated state for longer-lived reserved sessions (rare).

marta: failure modes: what happens if fence metadata lost while client reconnects? suggestion: fail closed (FORBID) to be safe, but maybe provide an operator override to allow degraded resume best-effort for low-risk endpoints.

nina: SLO/operational: accounting — we must charge ephemeral fence state memory to tenant quotas, and surface per-tenant fence churn alerts. also add dashboard for "replay_forbidden_rate" to detect backend commit races.

ops-bot: deploy-check: canary job for fence feature passed in staging (canary-42). Logs: fence.bind_success=1234 fence.bind_fail=12

aj: final call: does anyone object to moving this RFC to implementable PR? if not, I'll start a runtime patch for fence bookkeeping in the proxy and a small backend contract change to emit commit hooks.

marta: no objection. please include tests for eviction race and cross-region failover.

talia: +1. add a small migration note for Dedicated customers about tuning max_tenant_fences.

ben: awesome — thanks. I'll open the PR with TODOs and link tests. leaving open for 24h for late comments. :thumbsup:
